newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says 150 of its POWs released by Iran.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says 150 of its POWs released by Iran.

text.p: Iraq said on Saturday that its former foe Iran had freed 150 Iraqi prisoners of war jailed since their 1980-1988 war.
But the official Iraqi News Agency (INA), quoting a statement by Iraq's Foreign Ministry, said Baghdad wanted Iran to account for thousands more POWs.

"Iraq, while it highly appreciates the initiative, stresses that Iran is still detaining 20,000 Iraqi POWs registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross," INA quoted the statement as saying.
Iraq and Iran signed an agreement last year on mutual relations and the issue of POWs and remains of soldiers killed during the war, but did not announce the details.
Both have exchanged several hundred POWs and remains of soldiers. In August the remains of 400 Iraqis and 65 Iranians were delivered to army officials from the two countries.
Accounting for soldiers missing in action and POWs is among the thorniest issues hindering efforts to improve relations.
